fatal_errors: The response identifies coherent HEA multilayers generally rather than the specific λ = 16 nm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer with semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces.

It attributes the mechanism transition to increasing temperature, whereas the reported transition was observed during room-temperature nanoindentation and correlated with modulation period and interface coherency.
It reverses the key interfacial role: coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission, while semicoherent interfaces block glide and promote the proposed diffusion/interface-slip mechanism.
It replaces the actual modulation-period experiment and stress-exponent analysis with an unsupported hypothetical in situ high-temperature TEM experiment.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes that interface coherency can affect creep and mentions diffusion and dislocation glide, so it has limited topical alignment. However, it misses the central result: the approximately 16 nm-period Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer, containing semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces and misfit dislocations, produced the transition toward diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep and had the strongest reported creep resistance. The proposed high-temperature dependence is outside and inconsistent with the room-temperature testing boundary. No evidence is cited, no stress-exponent criterion is provided, and the suggested measurements would not by themselves cleanly discriminate atomic diffusion from interface slip or dislocation creep.
